title: The Book of Jonah Timeline
sub: Fleeing to Tarshish · Nineveh Repents, God Relents
desc: A prophet flees the mission he's given, is swallowed by a great fish, and finally preaches to Israel's enemy Nineveh — only to be furious when the city repents and God spares it, ending on an unanswered question about compassion for enemies.

eras.label: Era One · Jonah 1
eras.name: Fleeing to Tarshish — Thrown Into the Sea
eras.dates: Commanded to preach to Israel's enemy Nineveh, Jonah flees in the opposite direction and is swallowed by a storm of his own making

events.title: Go to Nineveh — Jonah Flees to Tarshish Instead
events.detail: Commanded to preach against Nineveh, the capital of Israel's brutal enemy Assyria, Jonah instead books passage in the opposite direction, fleeing toward Tarshish to escape the commission of the LORD [Yahweh].

verses.text: “Jonah immediately headed off to Tarshish to escape from the commission of the LORD [Yahweh]… to go with them to Tarshish, far away from the LORD [Yahweh].”

events.title: A Great Storm — Pagan Sailors Fear the LORD
events.detail: A violent storm threatens to break the ship apart; when the lot falls on Jonah and he confesses he's fleeing the LORD, the pagan sailors, more reverent than the prophet, reluctantly throw him overboard and the sea instantly calms.

verses.text: “The men feared the LORD [Yahweh] greatly and earnestly vowed to offer lavish sacrifices to the LORD [Yahweh].”

eras.label: Era Two · Jonah 2
eras.name: A Prayer From the Belly of the Fish
eras.dates: From the depths of the sea and the fish's stomach, Jonah prays a psalm of desperate thanksgiving. (The Hebrew text's chapter division falls one verse earlier than most English translations: the fish's appointment, told at the very end of chapter 1 in English Bibles, opens chapter 2 in the Hebrew numbering used here — shifting every following verse number in this chapter up by one, a versification difference only, not a different event. NET itself marks this boundary inline as “(2:1)” at the end of chapter 1.)

events.title: A Great Fish Appointed to Swallow Jonah
events.detail: The LORD [Yahweh] appoints a great fish to swallow Jonah, who remains in its stomach three days and three nights, a period later invoked by Jesus as a sign of his own coming death and resurrection. (Numbered 1:17 in most English translations; the Hebrew text used here opens chapter 2 with this verse instead.)

verses.text: “The LORD [Yahweh] sent a huge fish to swallow Jonah, and Jonah was in the stomach of the fish three days and three nights.”

events.title: Salvation Belongs to the LORD — Vomited Onto Dry Land
events.detail: From inside the fish, Jonah prays a psalm-like cry of distress and thanksgiving, remembering the LORD even from what he calls the belly of Sheol, and is vomited onto dry land when the LORD speaks to the fish.

verses.text: “Salvation belongs to the LORD [Yahweh]!” Then the LORD [Yahweh] commanded the fish and it vomited Jonah out onto dry land. (Numbered 2:9-10 in most English translations; 2:10-11 in the Hebrew numbering used here.)

eras.label: Era Three · Jonah 3
eras.name: Nineveh Repents — God Relents
eras.dates: A second commission, an eight-word sermon, and the most dramatic mass repentance in the Old Testament

events.title: The LORD's Message Came to Jonah a Second Time
events.detail: Given a second chance, Jonah finally obeys, entering the vast city of Nineveh and delivering the shortest recorded sermon in Scripture: forty days until overthrow.

verses.text: “At the end of 40 days, Nineveh will be overthrown!”

events.title: The People of Nineveh Believed — God Relented
events.detail: From the king down to the least citizen, all of Nineveh repents in sackcloth and fasting, and God [Elohim] relents from the destruction he had threatened, sparing Israel's greatest enemy.

verses.text: “When God [Elohim] saw their actions—that they turned from their evil way of living—God [Elohim] relented concerning the judgment he had threatened them with and did not destroy them.”

eras.label: Era Four · Jonah 4
eras.name: Jonah's Anger — Should I Not Be Concerned About Nineveh?
eras.dates: The book's real subject emerges: not Nineveh's repentance but Jonah's resentment of God's mercy toward his enemies

events.title: This Displeased Jonah Terribly — He Became Very Angry
events.detail: Rather than rejoicing, Jonah is furious that God spared Nineveh, revealing the real reason he fled in chapter one: he knew the LORD was gracious and feared exactly this outcome.

verses.text: “I knew that you are a gracious and compassionate God [El], slow to anger and abounding in mercy, and one who relents concerning threatened judgment.”

events.title: Should I Not Be More Concerned About Nineveh, This Enormous City?
events.detail: Using a plant that shades and then withers, the LORD confronts Jonah's misplaced compassion for a mere vine against his lack of compassion for 120,000 people, closing the book on an open, unanswered question.

verses.text: “Should I not be more concerned about Nineveh, this enormous city? There are more than 120,000 people in it who do not know right from wrong, as well as many animals.”
